placements.why: No strata exist yet in this repo. The content is a calibration record for the Kestrelwood spectrograph — an instrument's tuned value checked against a reference standard — which is organizational-category grain (how the org tracks instrument readiness), not itself a narrative theme. This mints the top-level Calibration category the org taxonomy names, instantiated here for the first time from real content.
placements.title: Instrument calibration as its own organizational category
placements.frame: Does this content report an instrument being brought into or confirmed within a calibrated, verified operating state?

placements.title: Calibration values are trusted only once checked against a named reference standard
placements.frame: What reference standard was this calibration checked against, and does the check hold across the full operating range?
placements.why: All three segments carry one directional claim (confirmed by the position pass): the Kestrelwood spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration is settled because it was verified against the June reference plates and holds across the full observing band. This is a subject future calibration envelopes will keep feeding — new instruments, new reference sets, new verification passes — not a one-time fact, so it clears the narrative grain test. No existing leaf or strata entry covers instrument-calibration verification (both sections are empty), so nothing to reuse; minted fresh under the newly-minted Calibration strata.
